answer.text: Official answer C; editorial worked explanation: For small angles, adjacent double-slit maxima are separated by Δθ≈λ/d. The graph’s narrow interference maxima are about 0.01 rad apart, so λ/d=0.01. The first minima of the broad single-slit envelope are at about ±0.10 rad, so λ/b=0.10. The pair is therefore 0.01 and 0.10, option C.
answer.evidence: Official May 2025 Physics HL Paper 1A TZ1 markscheme 2225-6707M, PDF page 3; editorial explanation independently checked against the complete original source question.

answer.text: Official answer D; editorial worked explanation: The grating spacing is d=1/(4.00×10⁵)=2.50×10⁻⁶ m. Maxima satisfy mλ=d sinθ, so |sinθ|≤1 requires m≤d/λ=2.50×10⁻⁶/(5.8×10⁻⁷)=4.31. The greatest integer order is 4. Orders −4 to +4 give 2(4)+1=9 maxima, including the central maximum. Hence D.
answer.evidence: Official May 2025 Physics HL Paper 1A TZ1 markscheme 2225-6707M, PDF page 3; editorial explanation independently checked against the complete original source question.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Which observation in a single-slit experiment supports the wave nature of monochromatic light?

A. Light travels straight through and produces one dot
B. Light bends and produces only one uniform band
C. Light is reflected at the slit edges
D. Light spreads and produces a series of bright and dark bands

answer.text: D. Diffraction and interference across the slit produce a broad central maximum and weaker side maxima separated by minima, supporting a wave model.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
The graph shows a double-slit interference pattern modulated by diffraction from the finite slit widths. What is the ratio of slit width to the distance between the slit centres?

A. 1/5
B. 1/4
C. 4
D. 5

answer.text: A. The interference maxima are separated by about 0.010 rad, while the first diffraction-envelope minimum is at about 0.050 rad. Since these angles are λ/d and λ/b, b/d=0.010/0.050=1/5.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The original source shows a monochromatic intensity pattern. Which combination of number of slits and slit width produces it? A. 1, width < λ  B. 1, width > λ  C. 2, width < λ  D. 2, width > λ

answer.text: Official answer D; editorial worked explanation: The regularly spaced narrow fringes show interference from two slits. Their heights are modulated by a broad single-slit diffraction envelope. The first envelope minima occur at angles smaller than 0.3 rad, so sin θ = λ/b is below 1 and the slit width b is greater than λ.
answer.evidence: Official May 2023 Physics HL Paper 1 TZ1 answer grid checked on PDF page 3; explanation independently calculated from the visible source question.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Which source pattern A-D is observed when white light passes through a diffraction grating?

answer.text: Official answer C; editorial worked explanation: At zero angle every wavelength has zero path difference, producing a central white maximum. On both sides, grating maxima are separated by wavelength: violet lies closest to the centre and red furthest away. The spectra are symmetric, matching C.
answer.evidence: Official May 2023 Physics HL Paper 1 TZ1 answer grid checked on PDF page 3; explanation independently calculated from the visible source question.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Light of wavelength λ diffracts through a rectangular slit of opening b. The source diagram shows rays from the same wavefront, and hence initially in phase, leaving the top and middle of the slit and reaching a distant point P at small angle θ. Show that their phase difference at P is πbθ/λ.

answer.text: Official markscheme derivation; editorial worked explanation: The two starting points are separated by b/2 across the slit, so their path difference is (b/2)sinθ≈bθ/2. A path difference Δx corresponds to phase difference Δφ=(2π/λ)Δx. Therefore Δφ=(2π/λ)(bθ/2)=πbθ/λ.
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics HL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6708M checked on PDF page(s) 14; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the source task.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The rays from the top and middle of the slit interfere destructively at P to form the first single-slit minimum. Explain why θ=λ/b.

answer.text: Official markscheme result; editorial worked explanation: Destructive interference for this top-to-middle pair requires phase difference π. Setting πbθ/λ=π gives bθ/λ=1, hence θ=λ/b. Equivalently, their path difference is λ/2, allowing the upper and lower halves of the slit to cancel pairwise.
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics HL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6708M checked on PDF page(s) 14; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the source task.

parts.given_text: Use the checked result from part (a)(i): the phase difference between these rays is Δφ=πbθ/λ.

notes: Superposition adds signed displacements, not speeds or frequencies. Opposite displacements can cancel while the waves continue to travel.
For pulses, first shift each shape by vt in its own travel direction, then add their heights point by point. After overlap, the original pulses continue unchanged in a linear medium.

original-ib26mb1a-mcq-22:whole.hint: Look for a pattern produced by superposition of contributions from different parts of the same slit.
notes: A single slit can produce an interference intensity pattern because different regions across the aperture contribute waves.
The central maximum is broader and brighter than the side maxima; spreading alone does not fully describe the observed band pattern.

original-ib26mc1a-mcq-20:whole.hint: Distinguish the narrow interference fringes from the broad diffraction envelope; compare their angular scales.
notes: For small angles, the separation of adjacent interference maxima is λ/d, while the first single-slit minimum is at λ/b.
A missing interference order occurs at the envelope minimum. Do not count only the visible peaks and mistake the fourth peak for that minimum.

fast-ib-a6e5d76baf5090c2-27:whole.hint: Separate the fine fringe spacing from the broad envelope: they reveal the number of slits and the individual slit width respectively.
notes: Two-slit interference produces repeated narrow maxima, while each slit supplies a broader diffraction envelope that controls their heights.
A first diffraction minimum at a real angle satisfies sin θ = λ/b, which requires b at least as large as λ and here greater than λ.

fast-ib-a6e5d76baf5090c2-28:whole.hint: Locate the zero-order maximum first, then use nλ = d sin θ to order colours by their diffraction angle on each side.
notes: All visible wavelengths overlap at the central zero-order maximum, so it appears white.
For the same order n, larger wavelength means larger diffraction angle; red is farther from the centre than violet.

fast-ib-996809f014b31dce-7-ai:whole.hint: First find the far-field path difference for points separated by b/2, then convert path difference to phase with 2π per wavelength.
notes: The two selected rays begin at the top and middle of the slit, so their separation is b/2 rather than b.
The distant-screen geometry makes the rays effectively parallel, and the small-angle approximation replaces sinθ with θ.

fast-ib-996809f014b31dce-7-aii:whole.hint: Set the supplied phase difference equal to the phase difference for destructive interference.
notes: A phase difference of π corresponds to a path difference of λ/2 for the paired rays.
At the first minimum, every point in one half of the slit can be paired with a point b/2 away in the other half, producing cancellation.
